newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher in early trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher in early trading.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to head higher in early trading, bolstered by some strength in high techs, the semiconductors in particular.

Analysts say the catalyst will be a report by the Semiconductor Industry Association forecasting semiconductor sales growth of 3.5 percent in the fourth quarter, an indication semiconductors might be pulling out of a year-long slump.
"This will be helpful to the chip-makers and it might give us a decent start," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
He said that the market was in a holding pattern ahead of Friday's October employment report and the November 5 U.S. Elections.
Investors will focus on today's October Chicago Purchasing Managers Index, due out at 1000 EST/1500 GMT and expected to come in at 54.0 compared to 56.3 the previous month.

"The Chicago PMI will be important because it foreshadows the National Association of Purchasing Management Index which is due tomorrow," Wachtel said. The opening will also depend on the latest weekly jobless claims report and September personal income and consumption, all due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
In Tokyo, The Nikkei fell 215 points to 20,467.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was down six at 3958.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, Texaco Inc was up 3/8 at 103-3/8 and Mobil Corp was up 3/8 at 118-3/8. Intel Corp was up 1/4 at 107, International Business Machines Corp rose 1/4 to 126-5/8 and Digital Equipment Corp was up 1/4 at 29. Homestake Mining Co rose 1/4 to 14-5/8.
U.S. Treasuries were higher, with the long bond up 6/32 to yield 6.69 percent.
The dollar dipped in Tokyo and was sturdier in Europe.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that shares of Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp have been falling on the stock market because investors expect it to make bid for Conrail Inc.
The New York Times Market Place writes that the difference between a small company selling for pennies a share and one selling for $9 is promotion, as shown by Chem International Inc.
